description: A Go CLI and the documented REST/Connect API let other scenarios and agents deliver an artifact to one of the owner's devices; all CLI commands emit structured JSON for scripting; the API contract is versioned and stable.

requirements.description: A Go CLI binary (device-sync CLI) allows other scenarios and agents to deliver files or text snippets to one of the owner's trusted devices by name or device_id. All CLI commands emit structured JSON output for scripting. The CLI authenticates using an owner API token (not interactive login). Commands include: send-file, send-text, list-devices, list-items. The CLI communicates with the hub's REST/Connect API. Flags: --device, --retention, --output=json|pretty. The CLI is distributed as a static binary with no runtime dependencies.
requirements.title: Programmatic Go CLI for Artifact Delivery

validation.notes: Unit test: send-file command constructs correct multipart upload request with filename, retention, and target device fields
Unit test: send-text command constructs correct JSON body with content, retention, and target device fields
Unit test: list-devices command outputs valid JSON array with id, name, and presence fields
Unit test: all commands return exit code 1 and JSON error object on API error response
Unit test: --output=json flag produces minified JSON; --output=pretty produces indented JSON
Integration test: run CLI send-file against a live hub instance; assert file appears in target device's item list
Integration test: run CLI list-devices; assert output matches devices returned by REST API
Integration test: run CLI with invalid API token; assert exit code 1 and JSON error with code=unauthorized
Documentation review: CLI --help output documents all flags and examples for send-file and send-text
Scripting test: pipe CLI list-devices output to jq; confirm valid JSON is parseable without errors

requirements.description: The hub exposes a versioned REST API (and optionally Connect/gRPC) enabling other scenarios and agents to deliver artifacts and manage devices programmatically. The API version is encoded in the URL path (e.g., /v1/). All endpoints are documented with request/response schemas. Breaking changes increment the major version. The API contract is stable within a major version: no request field removals, no response field removals, and no semantic changes without a version bump. The API is the canonical backend for both the web UI and the CLI.
requirements.title: Versioned REST/Connect API Contract for Programmatic Access

validation.notes: Unit test: all route registrations include the /v1/ prefix
Unit test: API response structs are validated against OpenAPI schema definitions in CI (schema contract test)
Unit test: no endpoint omits authentication middleware
Integration test: POST /v1/items with valid auth returns 201 and item metadata conforming to the documented schema
Integration test: unknown endpoint returns 404 with structured JSON error body
Integration test: schema contract test suite passes against a running hub instance with no violations
Documentation review: OpenAPI spec is published and covers all P0/P1 endpoints with request/response examples
Versioning review: confirm no v1 endpoint has changed its response schema without a version bump in the current release

title: Programmatic CLI & API Surface
